court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Gunvantrao Raghunath Patil And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Gunvantrao Raghunath Patil and others (husband, wife, relatives)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra and Jagruti Gunvantrao Patil (wife)

facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnized in 2011. The dispute has been amicably resolved and a decree of divorce has been executed on December 20, 2012.

legal_principles.principle: Continuation of prosecution in the face of an amicable settlement between parties would amount to abuse of process of law.
legal_principles.held: In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties, the likelihood of the prosecution ending in a conviction is very remote and bleak. Continuation of prosecution, in such circumstances, would amount to abuse of the process of the Court.

legal_principles.principle: A party's decision to settle a dispute and resolve the matter amicably should be respected by the court.
legal_principles.held: The Respondent No.2 - the First Informant admits that in pursuance of the settlement between the parties, the marriage has also been dissolved by decree of divorce passed in the month of January 2021.

outcome.final_order: The FIR registered with Sangvi Police Station, Pune for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506, 506(2) r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code is quashed and set aside.
